post_content:
Computer Vision vs NLP (with deep learning) if I show you a dog photo, you say
"its a dog" so does a neural network. infact, anyone who sees the same picture
will say "its a dog" Our hidden representation in our minds same for everyone.
Vision Networks can learn that or may be different. if I give a sentance, you,
me and everyone can have a different meaning figured out from it ( depends on
the context, knowledge, etc..) in this case our representation might be
completely different than each other's. neural networks can't learn that at
this point although we are making the machines learn . maybe we are yet to
discover new possibilities for NLP to achive that ability There is so much to
explore in NLP than vision, hope we will be giving that gift to our
generations and future. hashtag#machinelearning hashtag#deeplearning

profile_headline: Product @ Internshala | Ex - Frontbench| Ed-Tech Enthusiast | Guest Writer at Leading Digital Platforms
post_content:
I am getting surrounded by an inherent fear as people has started calling me
an Influencer on LinkedIn. May be, people have their choices and reasons to be
an Influencer, but it doesn't excite me. I don't want to be a social media
influencer. Interestingly, most successful people, are least active on social
media. I read a post where Ayush Jaiswal said, that a man keeps scrolling his
phone for 2 months in an year. This is scary. Two days back, I spent 4 hrs 12
mins, scrolling between different social media accounts. I prefer to be old
schooled. My heart still resides in scratching books with a pen and reading it
rather than use a Kindle. The average concentration span of a human being is
decreasing, as we are developing an inherent bias to keep scrolling things.
I'm not here to pass a verdict that social media is a boon or bane. But, I
guess, it's killing my productivity and creativity.
